title: WAYLIVRA® Post-Authorisation Safety Study (PASS) and Product Registry
summary:
WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THE STUDY?
This research study is being done at the request of the European Medicines Agency (EMA) to further characterise the safety and effectiveness of WAYLIVRA in patients with FCS (Familial Chylomicronaemia Syndrome) under real-world conditions.
The FCS treatment will be reviewed to see what effect they have on the patient as follows:
- To evaluate the safety of WAYLIVRA on severe thrombocytopenia (low platelet levels in the blood) and bleeding in FCS patients according to the dose recommendations.
- To evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety profile of WAYLIVRA, the health and quality of life of patients with FCS and how closely their prescribing doctor adheres to the dosing and platelet monitoring recommendations.
STUDY DESIGN
This is an observational safety study, which means information is collected from patient's medical records, and no experimental or extra treatments are done. All participants in this study have to be at least 18 years old and will receive WAYLIVRA according to the usual clinical practice followed by the prescribing physician, which may or may not be the Study Doctor of the patient. For the treatment with WAYLIVRA the platelets will be monitored at least every 2 weeks, and the patient will return to the clinic for visits every 3 months for safety and efficacy assessments as per standard of care. Participating in this study does not replace or change the patient's regular medical care. The patient's doctor may continue to prescribe WAYLIVRA to the patient during and after the study as long as the patient's doctor considers that the patient is benefitting from it. WAYLIVRA is not provided to the patient as part of this study. The prescription for WAYLIVRA is independent of patient's participation in this study.
This study will be conducted in two phases. The first phase of the study is the safety data phase and will be concluded after a study term of 5 years. Following the safety data phase, the study will continue as the WAYLIVRA Product Registry, or the Registry phase, which will be conducted throughout the commercial life of WAYLIVRA, to obtain long-term data.
Approximately 200 patients from France, Germany, Italy, The Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, the UK and other European countries will participate in this study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult patients (≥ 18-years-old) prescribed WAYLIVRA™ in accordance with the approved Summary of Product Characteristics.
2. Treated in Germany.
3. Have provided written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients for whom WAYLIVRA is not advised including:
• Patients with chronic or unexplained thrombocytopenia. Treatment should not be initiated in patients with thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 140 × 109/L).
• Patients with hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the following excipients:
o Sodium hydroxide (for pH adjustment).
o Hydrochloric acid (for pH adjustment).
